title: SPECIAL REPORT: Inside AI scam ads exploiting TikTok’s advertising system to defraud Nigerians

reading.body:
This is a case of impersonation carried out through paid advertising, where synthetic media was used to make fraudulent offers look like communications from real institutions and real people. The failure sits in the ad review and moderation layer of a platform's advertising system, not in a model's output alone: the ads were bought as promotions, ran for weeks, and reached users inside the normal ad experience. The deepfake videos and cloned voices were the delivery mechanism, and the fraud depended on the platform accepting and serving them.

Catching this would have required verification at the point of ad purchase, so that an advertiser cannot buy placement under a brand's or a public figure's identity. It would also have required detection of synthetic media in ad creative, and enforcement of the platform's own rules against scams and impersonation before the ads accumulated. The documented pattern, 130 ads over five weeks with comments disabled and no AI labels, indicates that review either did not run or did not act on what it saw.

What is not established is the intent or knowledge of any party beyond the ads themselves: the reporting documents the ads and the losses, and does not establish what TikTok or regulators will do, nor does it establish that any named brand or public figure participated in or authorised the promotions.

reports.title: SPECIAL REPORT: Inside AI scam ads exploiting TikTok’s advertising system to defraud Nigerians

summary:
A Premium Times investigation found that AI-generated scam ads are running as paid promotions on TikTok and defrauding Nigerians. The ads impersonate brands such as OPay, UBA, MTN and Airtel, and public figures including Aliko Dangote and the Emir of Kano, using deepfake videos and cloned voices. One victim, Mohammed Yusuf, lost about N150,000 after submitting his OPay details, while another, Ahmad Wura, lost roughly N1 million in cryptocurrency. The reporter documented 130 such ads over five weeks, most impersonating OPay, with comments disabled and no AI labels.

TikTok’s policies ban scams and impersonation, but the investigation found moderation gaps. Nigeria’s NITDA says Nigerians lose over $500 million yearly to scams. The article does not say what TikTok or regulators will do next, though experts called for stronger advertiser verification and digital governance.
